steps.text: Autumn, 1091
Rhodes Island of Babel, Kazdel

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: How's progress, Closure?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The last thing I need is another core system control failure.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Well... Heh, since you had to bring it up, I might have run into a little problem.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Even with the tricks you taught me, the encryption methods used by many of PRTS's programs are almost incomprehensible to a normal brain, and my decoder isn't fully compatible yet.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: We may not be able to shut the system down before the Doctor arrives on the ship.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Try again.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If you're not confident about getting it done, then we'll go to the contingency plan... cutting off power to the entire ship.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Leave it to me!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Seems like you're still keeping a lot of secrets, though.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I've never seen anyone make you so nervous.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...That's not important.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: What's important is making sure nothing happens to the ship.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Ascalon's report says the Doctor looks like an ordinary person. A pretty decent one, too, who picked up a stray little Cautus and carried her all across the land.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Do we really have to be so on edge?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It's not the Doctor that I fear.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Then what is it?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You don't need to know yet.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Wipe the Doctor's boarding records. This is for the safety of both the Doctor and Babel.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The others don't need to know that the Doctor exists until the Doctor and Theresa have reached a conclusion.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Alright, alright, I'll work at it.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: But I wonder why you seem to care a lot about this Doctor at that same time that you're so on guard over the whole thing.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I've got it! The Doctor must have dirt on you!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Don't bother, you won't find it.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Come on, why so serious?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: What about the girl?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Same conclusion, no change.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I cross-checked all relevant Rim Billitonian records and had Scout check with informants inside the Military Commission.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Amiya's background comes through clean.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Her parents were killed when the convoy transporting the laser mining module got attacked. The attack itself was purely coincidental.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: No one knew they were transporting Sarkaz-related cargo, and the Military Commission wasn't involved.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: She must have gotten Infected in the mess. If not for the Doctor, she'd be spending the rest of her life suffering in Rim Billiton.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I'll handle the girl's examination and treatment once she's on board.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: You're still concerned about her?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Yes, I am.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: She's too young, and she hasn't had proper treatment since contracting Oripathy.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Oh, that kind of concerned.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I don't want the Doctor's kindness to be the reason for delaying her treatment.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Plus, Theresa would call her a gentle child who has the right to choose her future.
Amiya. Amiya.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Mm... let me sleep... where are we?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor... Doctor?
The Doctor's here.
Wake up, sleepyhead. You're almost home.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Home?
In her half-awake state, Amiya feels a warm fingertip brush her cheek.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Haha, that tickles, don't do that, hehe.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Whoa!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Wh-Who are you?
I'm Theresa.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Theresa... the Doctor talked about you...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Oh? What did the Doctor say?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I don't remember... I was having a great carrot cake at the time, though.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Theresa should smell nice... be really warm and sweet...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: What about now? Is she as you imagined her?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Yeah... smells good... warm and sweet... doesn't smell like carrots, though...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Not fully awake, I see. Heh.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Will you come home with us, Amiya?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Home... yeah... okay...
Outside Rhodes Island of Babel, Kazdel
The tiny Cautus sleeps soundly in Theresa's arms, leading against her neck.
She pats Amiya on the back and turns toward the Doctor, who is clearly tired.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Thank you, Theresa. I didn't expect you to come pick us up personally.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Looks like you're not quite all-knowing, Doctor.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You have much to learn when it comes to childcare, at least.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Sure enough.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You look different from when you left, Doctor. How was the journey?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I saw a lot and learned a lot. There are plenty of interesting things on this great land.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I also met Amiya... it was a miracle that I was able to save her.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Amiya. She's even cuter than your letters said. Poor girl, but fortunate, in some way.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Her condition is getting worse. I needed to bring her in for treatment.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: How has Babel been, in the time that I was away?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Not quite smooth sailing. We have a lot to deal with, but not everything needs to be handled right away.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You must be tired after your journey. Get some rest.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Thank you, Theresa.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Amiya, we're home.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Hmm... Doctor? Did I fall asleep?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Oh, Amiya. You're awake.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Why don't you come down? Theresa will get tired if she has to keep holding you.
Amiya nods and jumps down from Theresa's arms.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Will you hold my hand, Amiya?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor...?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: It's alright. Theresa is my friend. You can trust her. You'll be spending a lot of time with her from now on.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Okay...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Is this Babel?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It's so big... even bigger than those mining plates. So this is where you used to live.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I spent a long time here... a very long time.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Is this your home?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Yes, Amiya, this is the Doctor's home. Right, Doctor?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: ...Yes.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It's your home now, too. Will you let us help the Doctor take care of you?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Alright... I'll go wherever the Doctor goes.
They step onto the elevator, and the Babel logo appears before their eyes.
The heavy door opens to welcome them in.
Sensing Amiya's unease, Theresa puts a hand on her shoulder.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: What's behind the door?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: People waiting to welcome you and the Doctor.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Are you sure about taking me and the girl in, Theresa?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Why shouldn't I be? I'm glad to have more people calling Babel their home.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Many here don't know you, though, so I'm sure you'll be busy for the next few days.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: How should I present myself?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Good question. You should talk to Kal'tsit first. She's been waiting for you.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Tell her your concerns, your questions, and the secrets in your heart.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: She would be very sad if you didn't.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: You could have...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: If you really want the King of Sarkaz to reveal the thoughts that you're loath to tell, I will. But I can feel you're still wavering.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Let's go, Amiya, Doctor. We'll go to her.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Amiya. You're Amiya, aren't you?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Yes...
Kal'tsit crouches down and gives the girl a candy.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Thank you for protecting the Doctor throughout your journey, Amiya.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Thank you... Dr. Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Will you fetch Theresa? We need to do some checks on you.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Will they hurt?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: A little. But the Doctor's letters called you a brave girl.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Will the Doctor be with me?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Of course. The Doctor has some things to do first, though.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: It's alright, Amiya. Just wait for me here in the ward, and I'll be back very soon.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: ...Okay.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You'll need to do a full checkup later too, Doctor.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...Doctor.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Yes?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Do you plan on leaving again?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: No, I think I've traveled enough.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If you've made up your mind, I'll respect your decision.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If nothing else, you're concerned about Amiya's health... even though she was a complete stranger to you.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: There is no fundamental difference between these new lives and us.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...I'm glad.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Glad that you chose hope, in the end.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Welcome back, Dr. {@nickname}.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: How is Amiya?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Blood Originium levels are high. Currently available inhibitors are not sufficient to stabilize her condition.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: We need to develop new drugs... I need time and resources.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Babel's are yours to use, Doctor. We're happy to share our research on Oripathy with you.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: What can I help you and Kal'tsit with in exchange?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: This is not a transaction. It's one of the core missions of Babel, to do everything in our power to help everyone suffering from Oripathy.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Since the day that Kal'tsit woke you up, I was convinced that you would help with all of this, just as you helped Amiya.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Now, perhaps, I have a chance to ask you this question, Doctor.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: How do you view this land, Terra?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I don't think it's my place to judge.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: There's no such thing as superior or inferior civilizations. It took a long and hard journey for Terra to evolve to where it is today.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Add to that the sick joke that Originium has played on life...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You said that Originium did not develop the way you expected.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: It wasn't supposed to bring such suffering.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: (Mumbles in her dream)

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I sense that you are keeping secrets, but there's nothing false about the sorrow coming from deep within your heart, the sorrow that I can't understand.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I want to fix this mistake, but I'm powerless to do so...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: At the end of the day, civilizations largely progress in similar ways. It all comes to an inevitable endpoint, however bright its light shines at its peak.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But Kal'tsit said you didn't give up hope, even in your final days.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I had many friends, even in those last days, who faced difficulties far greater than you can imagine, with courage and hope that is every bit your equal.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: But they failed and faded away, without exception.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: We haven't known each other that long, Theresa. I want to know: Why do you do all this?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: What is the end that Babel seeks in compromising with the Military Commission?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: There's something I want to show you, Doctor.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: We had to ask you about Originium, sooner or later. That's why Kal'tsit woke you up.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Please, come and see the results of my... brief time at work.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: We're almost there...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: This place is barren, even by the standards of a Catastrophe-heavy region. But Closure has spent time and effort to maintain this dangerous little trail...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: A forked trail in the midst of Originium formations. You're not keeping any fewer secrets than I am, Theresa.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: A King of Sarkaz has to have a few secrets, right?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Don't tell anyone what you see here.
A long trek through the Originium-filled wasteland leads to a small garden.
In the heart of a Catastrophe, amidst the ruins, on a nameless plain that neither night nor the stars can find.
Tiny white specks mark this little sanctuary, isolated from the rest of the world, and the wild lands around it. Even the winds seem softer here.
It is a forgotten greenhouse that harkens back to a time in the distant past, when the land was still pure and untainted.
Like when man stole fire from up above and lit up a corner of the night sky.
Theresa picks up a white flower.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: This place represents the cutting edge of Babel's and my research into Originium.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Flowers...?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: No. Originium.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I'm sure you understand it's not Originium Arts that made these flowers bloom.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: The information inherent in Originium, the reversal of the Assimilated Universe...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: You've already come this far? When did...?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: No race understands Originium better than the Sarkaz. Still, what we know is merely the tip of the iceberg compared to the entirety of Originium.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Even with Kal'tsit helping us understand the nature of Originium, the furthest we have gone is transforming a palm-sized piece of active Originium into this...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Garden.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Hope.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: This little flower is my small contribution. I need your help, Doctor.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I want to see the day when flowers cover the cliffs and valleys of Kazdel, and all the lands beyond.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It's a future worth taking risks for.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You've seen how Kazdel has been mired in war for its entire history, Doctor.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Right now, at least, I want to use the power of Originium to create a home for Kazdel where people can live in peace, safe from war and invasion.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: In the more distant future... if we're able to fully harness it, we'll be able to change the entire face of Terra.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: If Catastrophes don't bring rain of Originium, but soft fluffy clouds...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: If the Infected no longer suffer the pain of rocks growing out of them...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I don't suppose there's anyone who would have such an absurd dream.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: You're different from other Sarkaz, Theresa.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Flowers that cover the entire land...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: What a picture of life that would be.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Doctor?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Why... why this flower?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Oh... there's no particular reason. I just happened to come across it outside the valley when I was looking for a good place for my experiments.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: A pure coincidence.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Kal'tsit said it had a name. 'Snow-in-summer'.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But it's adapted to changes over the years. Perhaps we could give it a new name.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: What do you think, Doctor?

a.text: A new path is opening up.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Can you hear me, Theresa?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I'm listening. I was giving the Doctor a tour of our...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Urgent news from Kazdel.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It concerns Victoria.
